bits/2903658:
Pure engine work, no UI. Every case here is one the plan's architect
review caught by reading the code, and each would have shipped a bug into
bit files already on someone's phone.

Flip is a frame transform, not a canvas mirror. Pass samples are stage
coordinates, not local, so they do not mirror with the puppet, and
localToWorld/worldToLocal knew nothing about flip. A draw-time scale(-1,1)
would have put a dragged pin at the mirror image of the finger and swung
snipped pieces the wrong way. Flip now lives in the local/world pair, the
sim mirrors the piece rest angle and the dangle coupling, the drawer
mirrors after the root frame so mouths, eyes, pieces and the MLS warp all
follow, and text keeps its letters legible while its position mirrors.
Proven in pixels: the ink centroid lands the same distance the other side
of centre, to within a third of a percent.

A reorder survives the next drag. castOf builds order from Map insertion
and every CAST re-inserts, so the first touch after a reorder would have
silently undone it. Draw order is now the latest REORDER filtered to live
puppets, then everything it does not name in latest-CAST order, which with
no REORDER in the log is exactly the old rule.

Pin and snip indices are slots that never compact. Six call sites pair by
that index, so filtering a removed pin out of the list would re-target
every later pass. Removal nulls the slot, a freed slot is never reused,
and PIN carries an optional index so a pin can be moved without orphaning
its passes. Snips work the same way, riding the skip splitPieces already
had. Exclusivity counts live snips, so removing the last cut makes a
puppet pinnable again and restores the pins it had before.

Undo pops a whole group and redo restores it in order. Undo popping a
group while redo pushed one event back would have re-applied half a
compound edit.

Also: MUTE, TRIM and REMOVE on passes, all ignored gracefully when their
target is absent, because corpse recording simulates a project
stoop/29bd225:
Two voices replace the pen. Hand was a cursive system font, which is a
birthday card. Marker is the fat pen: heavy, each word turned by its own
small angle, from a hash so the screen and the paper agree. Stencil is
Impact with the bridges cut through it at a fixed interval of the type
size, the way a sprayed letter has to be held together; on screen it is a
mask so it needs no font nobody has, on paper each line is drawn once per
band of ink, clipped to it. Older issues that say hand read as marker.

Stamps are the grammar of the form, ready cut: FREE, TAKE ONE, PHOTOCOPY
THIS, the number sign, an arrow, a star, a strip of tape, a staple, and a
barcode that scans nothing. Each is one small description in a unit box
(polygon, rect, outline, line, text), and the same description is drawn
as SVG on the screen and as path operators on paper, so the two cannot
drift. The barcode's bars come from a hash. A palette under + STAMP glues
one to the page last touched, slightly crooked.

GENERATION is how many times the issue has been through the copier:
master, a copy, a copy of a copy, laundromat. On screen it is an SVG
filter on every page but the one being typed into, fraying edges and
throwing toner. It is recorded on the issue when the bell rings and
travels in the file, so a reprint wears the same generation. On paper it
is speckle over every panel and dust and dropout in the photographs,
drawn from fixed seeds so every print of the issue wears the same marks.

A text cutting's box is sized to the screen's layout in a condensed face;
the paper face runs wider and may wrap a line longer. The PDF used to
drop that line. A cutting now hangs over its box instead, up to a little
more than half its height, which is what a glued cutting does anyway.
